'''Samuel Peterson "P. J." Hairston Jr.''' (born December 24, 1992) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina Tar Heels]]. He finished his sophomore season in 2013 and was eligible for the [[2014 NBA draft]].<ref name="d-league">{{cite web|first=Jeff|last=Goodman|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/10276003/pj-hairston-submits-paperwork-nba-development-league|title=P.J. Hairston hopes to join D-League|work=ESPN.com|date=January 10, 2014|access-date=January 13, 2014}}</ref> He was selected with the 26th overall pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]] by the [[Miami Heat]], and was later traded to the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in exchange for [[Shabazz Napier]].

==High school career==
Hairston attended [[James B. Dudley High School|Dudley High School]] in Greensboro for his first three years of high school. He scored 53 points in one game as a junior. For his senior year of high school, he played at [[Hargrave Military Academy]] in [[Chatham, Virginia]] and averaged 25.6 points, 9.2 rebounds, and 4.7 assists. He scored 15 points in the [[2011 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]].<ref name=bio>{{cite web|url=http://www.goheels.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=205497519|title=P.J. Hairston Biography|work=GoHeels.com|access-date=December 20, 2013}}</ref>

Considered a five-star recruit by [[ESPN.com]], Hairston was listed as the No. 3 shooting guard and the No. 13 player in the nation in 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/66496/pj-hairston|title=P. J. Hairston Recruiting Profile|work=ESPN.com|access-date=December 20, 2013}}</ref>

==College career==
In 2011, Hairston joined the [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina Tar Heels]] for the 2011–12 season as a freshman. He was the team's eighth-leading scorer at 5.7 points per game and led the team in free-throw percentage.<ref name="bio" />

In the 2012–13 season, Hairston's playing time increased significantly in the second half of the season. In the last five games of the regular season, he averaged 32 minutes of playing time, up 60% from 20 minutes of average playing time in the first 29 games of the season. Hairston led UNC in scoring in the last five games of the season with 19.6 points per game. He earned ACC Co-Player of the Week honors for his play against Duke and Virginia in February 2013. North Carolina coaches also selected Hairston as the defensive player of the game in the win over Virginia.<ref name="bio" />

In Hairston's sophomore season, he was in the starting line-up for the second time in his college career against Duke in February 2013. He scored a then career high 23 points. In his next game in the starting line-up versus Virginia he set a new high with 29 points, just four games after returning the court after missing a game due to a concussion. In UNC's first game of the ACC tournament on March 15, 2013, Hairston was holding the basketball in the second half when a Florida State player swiped Hairston's hand. Either from the swipe, or from his fingers extending on the basketball, Hairston split the webbing between the middle and ring fingers on his non-shooting left hand.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/basketball/ncaa/men/gameflash/2013/03/15/85456/index.html#matchup |title=North Carolina tops Florida State 83-62 in ACCs |work=SportsIllustrated.CNN.com |date=March 15, 2013 |access-date=March 15, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140113210715/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/basketball/ncaa/men/gameflash/2013/03/15/85456/index.html#matchup |archive-date=January 13, 2014 }}</ref> Hairston left the game and received eight stitches. He still led UNC with 21 points after making five of six three point shots.

After getting the stitches, Hairston returned to play in UNC's next two games in the ACC tournament. He played 36 minutes in the next game against Maryland and scored 13 points. In the next day's game against Miami he scored 28 points.

Suspended in 2013, Hairston did not return to North Carolina for the 2013–14 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/10271516/pj-hairston-not-enrolled-spring-semester-north-carolina|title=P.J. Hairston not enrolled at UNC|work=ESPN.com|date=January 9, 2014|access-date=January 9, 2014}}</ref> On December 20, 2013, the school announced that they would not seek his reinstatement.<ref>{{cite web|first=C. L.|last=Brown|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/10172154/north-carolina-tar-heels-not-applying-ncaa-reinstatement-pj-hairston|title=Tar Heels won't seek reinstatement|work=ESPN.com|date=December 20, 2013|access-date=December 20, 2013}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Texas Legends (2014)===
After his suspension was confirmed, Hairston filed paperwork to join the [[NBA Development League]].<ref name="d-league" /> On January 14, 2014, he was acquired by the [[Texas Legends]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/texas/pj_hairston_2014_01_14.html|title=LEGENDS ACQUIRE PJ HAIRSTON|work=NBA.com|date=January 14, 2014|access-date=January 14, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Bobby|last=Karalla|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/texas/legends_claim_pj_hairston_2014_01_14.html|title=Legends Claim P.J. Hairston|work=NBA.com|date=January 14, 2014|access-date=January 14, 2014}}</ref> He went on to play 26 games for Texas while averaging 21.8 points, 3.5 rebounds and 1.5 steals per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/dleague/players/h/hairspj01d.html |title=PJ Hairston Jr. D-League Stats |work=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=June 30, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150912214452/http://www.basketball-reference.com/dleague/players/h/hairspj01d.html |archive-date=September 12, 2015 }}</ref>

===Charlotte Hornets (2014–2016)===
On June 26, 2014, Hairston was selected with the 26th overall pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]] by the [[Miami Heat]] on behalf of the [[Charlotte Hornets]]. In doing so, Hairston became the first NBA D-League player to be drafted in the first round of an NBA draft.<ref>{{cite web|first=James|last=Herbert|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nba/eye-on-basketball/24598799/nba-draft-charlotte-hornets-get-an-a-for-picking-pj-hairston-at-no-26|title=2014 NBA Draft: Hornets get A for landing P.J. Hairston in a trade at No. 26|access-date=June 27, 2014|date=June 26, 2014|work=CBSSports.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Anthony|last=Oliva|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/pj_hairston_drafted_2014_06_26.html|title=Hairston Becomes First NBA D-League Alum Picked in First Round of NBA Draft|access-date=June 27, 2014|date=June 26, 2014|work=NBA.com|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140628091445/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/pj_hairston_drafted_2014_06_26.html|archive-date=June 28, 2014}}</ref> On August 22, he signed with the Hornets after averaging an impressive 18.3 points in seven Summer League games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/hornets-sign-hairston|title=Hornets Sign Hairston|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=August 22, 2014|access-date=August 22, 2014}}</ref> On December 22, Hairston recorded his first career double-double with 10 points and 10 rebounds to help the Hornets defeat the [[Denver Nuggets]], 110–82.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141222/DENCHA/gameinfo.html|title=Hornets top Nuggets 110-82 for third straight win|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=December 22, 2014|access-date=December 22, 2014}}</ref> On February 10, 2015, he scored a season-high 16 points in a loss to the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/hairspj02/gamelog/2015/|title=P.J. Hairston 2014-15 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=June 30, 2015}}</ref>

On June 30, 2015, Hairston re-joined the Hornets for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/hornets-announce-2015-orlando-pro-summer-league-roster|title=Hornets Announce 2015 Orlando Pro Summer League Roster|work=NBA.com|date=June 30, 2015|access-date=June 30, 2015}}</ref> On January 23, 2016, he scored a then career-high 20 points and tied a career-high with 10 rebounds in a 97–84 win over the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160123/NYKCHA/gameinfo.html|title=Lin, Walker lead Hornets past Knicks 97-84|work=NBA.com|date=January 23, 2016|access-date=January 23, 2016}}</ref>

===Memphis Grizzlies (2016)===
On February 16, 2016, the Hornets traded Hairston to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in a three-way deal also involving the [[Miami Heat]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/anderson-and-hairston-aquired-in-trade-160216|title=Grizzlies acquire four 2nd Round Picks, Chris Andersen & P.J. Hairston in three-team trade|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=February 16, 2016|access-date=February 16, 2016}}</ref> He made an impression early for the Grizzlies, earning the starting shooting guard role and subsequently scoring 17 points on February 24 against the Los Angeles Lakers in just his third game for the team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/hairspj02/gamelog/2016/|title=P.J. Hairston 2015-16 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=February 27, 2016}}</ref> He went on to score a career-high 21 points on February 26, helping the Grizzlies defeat the Lakers for the second time in three days.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160226/MEMLAL/gameinfo.html|title=Carter scores 19 for Grizzlies in 112-95 win over Lakers|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=February 26, 2016|access-date=February 27, 2016}}</ref>

===Rio Grande Valley Vipers (2016–2017)===
On September 30, 2016, Hairston signed with the [[Houston Rockets]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/rockets/rockets-sign-free-agent-pj-hairston|title=Rockets Sign Free Agent P.J. Hairston|work=NBA.com|date=September 30, 2016|access-date=September 30, 2016}}</ref> but was waived on October 24, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-waive-three-players|title=Rockets Waive Three Players|work=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2016|access-date=October 24, 2016}}</ref> Seven days later, he was acquired by the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] of the [[NBA Development League]] as an affiliate player of the Rockets.<ref>{{cite web|first=Anwar|last=Chagollan|url=http://riograndevalley.dleague.nba.com/news/vipers-perform-trade-erie-finalize-training-camp-roster/|title=Vipers perform trade with Erie and finalize training camp roster|work=NBA.com|date=October 31, 2016|access-date=November 2, 2016}}</ref>

Hairston announced his retirement from basketball in 2018, having been out of the game for a season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wralsportsfan.com/former-unc-guard-pj-hairston-announces-end-of-basketball-career-/17696655/|title=Former UNC guard PJ Hairston announces end of basketball career|work=wralsportsfan.com|date=July 13, 2018|access-date=July 15, 2018}}</ref>
